newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index eases in selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index eases in selective trade.

text.p: The Kuwaiti share index fell 13.1 points to 2,197.3 in the week ending Wednesday in selective trade as some shares continued to correct following large gains in March, dealers said on Thursday.
"Trade focused on safe shares. The value of some shares fell as the market continued to adjust prices," said a portfolio manager. "Nothing out of the ordinary."
Losers led gainers 28-15, while 18 shares were unchanged.
"The market will start an upwards trend in the coming weeks," said a private dealer.
In the first quarter of 1997 the index and trade levels registered several peaks mainly due to capital flows from abroad to invest in listed firms which showed profit increases in 1996.

The daily average for value of traded shares rose to 38.1 million dinars ($125.7 million) from 35.4 million. Volume rose to a daily average of 184 million shares from 154 million, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday show.
Real estate firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 75 million dinars, followed by investment firms with 58 million and non-Kuwaiti companies with 30 million.
United Realty, Kuwait Real Estate, Umm al-Quwain Cement National Investments, Investment Projects, and Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
